score.note: Second pass, evidence-grounded (not permutation). Fixed the work/draw_destination read from two independent *(void**)0x03001EEC / *(void**)0x03001EF0 dereferences to the cursor-advance idiom already used by the adopted 080ce85c.c sibling (`cursor = ...; work = *cursor++; draw_destination = *cursor;`), which matches the reference's `ldmia r3!, {r2}` and pulls matched_prefix from 7 to 12 instructions immediately. Then found and fixed a real semantic bug: the inner j-loop's velocity_a/velocity_b arguments (passed to Func_08004c1c/Func_08004bd4/Func_08004c6c) are NOT loop-invariant per outer pass as the previous draft modeled -- the retained assembly's .L2 loop-bottom block increments r8/r9 by +-(outer<<3) on every one of the 64 inner-loop passes, unconditionally (both the gated and ungated path reach .L2), so velocity_a actually equals (outer<<8) + j*(outer<<3) at iteration j, not a constant outer<<8. Rewrote as `velocity_a = outer<<8` once per outer pass, `velocity_b = -velocity_a` recomputed fresh at the top of every j iteration, and `velocity_a += outer<<3` at the loop bottom (letting the GCC 2.96 backend's own induction-variable strength reduction turn the C-level accumulation into the same kind of running-total the reference already shows for its own outer-loop-level accumulators elsewhere in this file, e.g. the sl-based -256/outer pass step visible in the pre-fix compile). This is the single largest structural finding this pass and should be treated as settled: differing_halfwords going from 263 (old, wrong-semantics baseline) to 277 (new, correct-semantics candidate) is a real but small regression traded for actual correctness, not noise -- do not revert to the constant-velocity model.

family.velocity_growth_finding: The inner j-loop's velocity arguments are NOT constant per outer pass: the retained assembly increments r8 (velocity_b, initialized to -(outer<<8)) and r9 (velocity_a, initialized to outer<<8) by -+(outer<<3) at the bottom of EVERY one of the 64 j-iterations (label .L2, reached unconditionally regardless of whether the gated draw code fired that iteration). velocity_a_j = (outer<<8) + j*(outer<<3); velocity_b_j is always exactly -velocity_a_j. This is worth checking against 080d59b0/080d82b0/080e7404 if any of them have a similar per-outer-pass velocity/angle argument passed into a small dispatch of 3-4 callees selected by (loop_index & 3) -- the same growth pattern likely recurs.
family.register_pressure_lever: Concrete lever confirmed this pass: expressing the per-iteration velocity growth as `velocity_a += outer << 3;` (recomputed inline, no named intermediate) at the loop bottom, combined with computing velocity_b fresh via `velocity_b = -velocity_a;` at the top of each iteration (NOT as its own independent accumulator incremented by -outer<<3), keeps this compiler's register allocator inside the budget that lets `work` stay in fp for the whole function. Every variant tried that gave velocity_b its OWN persistent accumulator (whether via `velocity_b += -outer<<3` directly, via a named `neg_outer` variable, or via two independent inductions) pushed `work` out of fp entirely into a stack spill (regressing to candidate=640-664, differing_halfwords=288-302), even though the reference itself DOES use two independent accumulators (r8 and r9 both incrementing). This compiler's specific allocator does not tolerate the same register pressure our source produces for a functionally-identical dual-accumulator formulation, so the single-accumulator-plus-fresh-negation shape, despite being structurally different from the reference's r8/r9 pair, is the better regression-free way to express this pattern under real register pressure. Still short of matching reference's exact fp=work/sl=outer/r8=velocity_b/r9=velocity_a/r6=star/r7=j register assignment (candidate lands on fp=work/r9=outer/sl=velocity_a/r8=j/r7=star instead) -- worth a future pass with more register-allocation experimentation budget.

rejected_experiments: Explicit `neg_outer = -outer;` variable (mirroring the reference's spilled -outer at sp+8) combined with either the accumulate-style or multiply-style velocity update: regressed `work` out of fp every time (matched_prefix dropped from 12 back to 7), regardless of where the variable was declared (function scope vs block scope -- declaration order/scope had zero measured effect on this compiler's allocation, only the actual computational shape mattered).

`velocity_a = (outer<<8) + j*(outer<<3)` computed fresh every iteration (letting the compiler's strength reduction alone do the work, no manual accumulation): produces the correct semantics and the compiler DOES strength-reduce it into a running accumulator, but this shape still regressed `work` out of fp (candidate=640, dh=290) -- worse than the manual single-accumulator-plus-negation shape (candidate=624, dh=277).

Two independent accumulators (`velocity_a += step; velocity_b -= step;`, with or without a named hoisted `step = outer<<3`): regressed to candidate=644-664, dh=288-302, always by evicting `work` from fp -- this is the shape closest to what the reference's own r8/r9 registers literally do, but this compiler cannot afford it alongside everything else without spilling `work`.

Swapping which of velocity_a/velocity_b is the persistent accumulator (`velocity_b` as accumulator, `velocity_a = -velocity_b` fresh): candidate=628, dh=283 -- slightly worse than velocity_a-as-accumulator (dh=277), kept the latter.

do-while vs for loop shape for the inner j-loop, tried both before and after the velocity-growth fix: zero measured effect on differing_halfwords in either case for this specific loop. (Earlier session hint that loop shape 'changes which locals get spilled' did not reproduce here.)

Semantic summary (revised): a single-target (not per-member-list) battle-presentation sub-effect. Seeds a 256-slot particle pool at 0x02010000 with random signed positions and zeroed velocity/lifetime fields, sets up one fixed 3-word draw record (0,160<<15,0), then runs 160 animation passes. Each pass re-establishes the facing/portrait draw, computes a per-pass base velocity pair (velocity_a = outer<<8, velocity_b = -velocity_a) and then walks the first 64 pool slots; velocity_a/velocity_b GROW by +-(outer<<3) every one of those 64 sub-steps regardless of whether a slot fires, so the velocity kick applied to a firing slot depends on both the outer pass number and how far into the 64-slot inner walk it is. Once a slot's activation threshold (a function of its index divided by 4) is crossed and it is still marked inactive, it fires one of four velocity-kick calls selected by (index & 3) using the current velocity_a/velocity_b, transforms it through Func_080e3944, clamps and buckets the transformed distance into a lookup-table draw offset, and draws it via Func_080072f4; independently, once a slightly later threshold is crossed, the slot's position is decayed by a shifted, negated velocity term every pass (simple drag).

Two open questions carried over from the earlier owners in this family and still not resolved: the observed 5th-argument-in-r4 calling convention at the Func_080072f4 site (confirmed this pass to be a genuinely unprecedented direct-call ABI quirk, not something any adopted sibling has actually solved -- see rejected_experiments), and getting this compiler to match the reference's exact fp=work/sl=outer/r8=velocity_b/r9=velocity_a/r6=star/r7=j register assignment rather than the leaner-but-different fp=work/r9=outer/sl=velocity_a/r8=j/r7=star assignment this candidate currently produces.
No GS2 or external source was used; no other Golden Sun decompilation project was consulted.
